title: Wagertech <> Jumpr - 60 Min (Joyce Kiddell)

items.statement: The PRD fields are to be captured as data, not necessarily surfaced to users. WagerTech wants condensed, more digestible views built from the rep's point of view first.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: But the goal was always to just ensure that the data is being captured against it, not necessarily that it's being like surfaced to the user, right, as they're navigating through the system. So, um, our hope is to like be able to condense the views a lot more, / Joyce Kiddell: just make it like, um, more digestible, you know, primarily from the lens of a rep. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Absolutely.

items.topic: Apply end-user lens before client review
items.statement: WagerTech expects Jumpr to apply the end-user (rep) lens to the other screens before WagerTech takes time to review them. Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: And our hope is that, you know, before we kind of move into um, reviewing the other screens that you guys are able to actually take that same lens and be like, okay, what would the end user actually want to see? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Absolutely.

items.statement: Kobi stated the screens shown so far are the admin view with all fields for this phase. Role-based page layouts and permission sets can tailor and hide fields for reps.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I mean I think I mentioned this in our last call like the the screens you're seeing is more or less the admin view right it's all the fields that uh we thought was important for this phase um but not necessarily the final view that the reps will see we can create uh different page layouts um that's going to be tailored based on your role the permissions that you have

items.statement: Even for admins, screens should use hints or tooltips (for example to mark a section as read only) and remove duplicate fields that appear in different blocks.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: a couple things we can do even for admins right like making it clear with like some like hints or tool tips to be like you know this section is read only for example or um there were examples of like kind of duplicate fields in different like blocks on a screen. So I'm like okay let's like get rid of that like try to like condense it even more that way. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, that that works. That works.

items.topic: UI labels match ERD and dictionary
items.statement: UI labels must line up with the ERD and data dictionary. Legacy labels from the existing API (for example 'book name') are to be replaced to match the go-forward model.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I want to make sure that we're approaching it from the lens of like whatever um, labels we have in the UI should line up with what's in the erd. in our like data dictionary, you know what I mean? Where it's like there were a couple examples of like book name and I know that's I'm sure holds from our existing API. / Joyce Kiddell: but like if you can just make sure that's part of your process and your build and that like just scrap whatever was s***** before and make sure it's more uniform with like the the go forward plan that you already kind of know about, right? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, that that works. That works.

items.statement: Joyce stated the project is about week two going into the build.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Okay. Um, and yeah, it's it I know this is like week two kind of going into the build too

items.topic: Rename study link clicks to leads
items.statement: Joyce proposed calling study link clicks 'leads' and calling repeat attempts on the same player/deal/market combination 'clicks' (many clicks per lead). Kobi deferred feedback; no explicit agreement on the naming.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: this is what we're envisioning um for study link clicks. I'd rather call them leads. / Joyce Kiddell: I think those are going to be called clicks because you can have multiple clicks against one lead, / Kobi Kunasekaran: It does. Let's keep going and then I will I'll come back and provide some feedback.

items.topic: Lead queue statuses For Review and Archived
items.statement: In Joyce's mockup the lead queue has only 'For review' (default for new clicks) and 'Archived' (not a real signup but kept for record). Later superseded in direction by the single-object status model.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: and then the only statuses would be like for review and for review would be like defaults because it's like all of the the new clicks that have come through and they haven't taken a look at. archived are ones where it's like, okay, we like the rep will know that this sign up or this um click lead, whatever, does not turn into a real signup. So, I'm just going to like put it aside, but we still want record of it.

items.statement: The queue should not show record IDs. It should show player first and last name plus the operator and partner combination.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: instead of having the IDs because like our team is not going to respond to having like IDs in your face like this like I will guarantee right now. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. Yeah. / Joyce Kiddell: so I changed it to just first and last name and then the combination of operator and partner, which I think you already have.

items.statement: Joyce proposed ordering the queue by recency, showing relative dates (for example '5 days ago') up to one week, then the actual date.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, and then just like recency um, ordered, right? Um, where it's like I think up until uh, a week would would be the rule that I'd prefer. Um, it would be like um, you know, 5 days ago, six days ago, and then when you hit like more than a week later or earlier, it'll just default to the the date itself, you know.

items.topic: Lead detail shows attribution and key player info
items.statement: The lead detail panel should show attribution and quickly relevant player information (signup date, age). Deeper player details (address, postal code, city) are seen by clicking through to the player record. Joyce said the field list still needs pressure testing.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: and then just broke it down into like the two things that uh are like good for us to be able to know and that like okay, where did this come from? Like what's the attribution associated with this lead? and then all the information that's quickly relevant about the player, / Joyce Kiddell: Um, that would be helpful to see once you actually click on the player name, right? Like you can go deeper on that record, but you don't need to see it here.

items.topic: Click history reorders by latest click
items.statement: A history list should show all clicks with the same permutation, and the lead should move to the top of the list on the most recent click attempt.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: and then yeah, this would be like a running list of all the clicks that have the same kind of permutation. Um, and then my log would be that everything like this this list reorders depending on the most recent click attempt. / Joyce Kiddell: It just gets bumped to the top if they do it again kind of thing.

items.statement: In the mockup the lead record is clearly read only, and the rep either archives it or progresses it to signup from the record.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, and then the making it clear that it's read only. Um and then you can either archive it uh or you progress to sign up by clicking it here.

items.topic: Bulk archive and hover quick actions
items.statement: Joyce asked for bulk editing (at least bulk archive of selected records; bulk sign-up likely not needed) and hover quick actions to view, archive, or move to signup. Kobi later committed only to test bulk edit feasibility.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um, and then I don't I think this is possible, but the concept of like bulk editing, right, where you can archive everything that's been selected or or um maybe you cannot sign them up because that doesn't make sense to do them all at once, but at least archive um and then hovering over each one where it's like okay like do I just want to view it because you can actually edit it? Do I want to archive it or do I want to move it to sign up?

items.statement: Kobi described the current build: study link clicks are a staging area for incoming API payloads; a signup record is created for each unique study link click combination, and duplicates roll up into the existing signup record.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um right now what we have built is yeah like the study click links are essentially the uh like the staging area for all the clicks that are coming in and they get converted into or not converted but uh signup records are created uh when it's like a unique study click link / So if there are duplicates it'll just roll up into that same ex existing signup record.

items.statement: WagerTech requires an explicit rep action to move an automatically created lead into a signup, so the signup queue is not cluttered with dead records. Jumpr agreed to deliver this as a step within the same object.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: but I I think like there has to be some sort of like trigger or action on the rep's end to move it from a lead to a sign up. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Like if the whole concept is just simplified interface and an explicit step for / Kobi Kunasekaran: the rep to move that uh lead version of the signup to an actual signup, we can still achieve it within the same object.

items.statement: Future state: data from WagerTech (post-back or proof data) could automatically move a lead to a signup. For now reps must be able to progress leads manually.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: but there's going to be our ideal state is a world where we're sending you an autom like a data point that pushes it into the signup. So then like when they're looking in that signup view like it's very intentional like you know what I mean like and it's going to be refined but they still need the ability to to progress manually
items.critic_note: Line range tightened from 306-385 to 385 (quote is Emily's line 385 only); timestamp corrected to 00:21:58. Joyce's 'Post box' at line 306 = postback [ASR?].

items.statement: WagerTech wants a bucket of leads that did not progress, to enable follow-up (for example email) and to project or report on how many do not convert.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: concept of leads being separate so that like we actually have a bucket of like hey these are the people who actually didn't like make it through to the next step. So, like let's hit them up with like an email or something, you know,

items.topic: Single Signup object with lead status
items.statement: Leads and signups will be one Signup object, with a lead status/stage, instead of a separate Lead object. Kobi proposed it to avoid conversion, duplicate and lookup logic; Joyce accepted as long as the end-user result is the same.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I think we can still do it in one object to combine both leads and signup. Uh because we could introduce another stage uh or status called lead status. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, if it's the same object, I don't really care to be honest. Like as long as we get to like the same kind of like end user results. / Joyce Kiddell: stage a stage makes sense to me.
items.supersedes_hint: Joyce's mockup proposed a separate leads concept/tab; Kobi: 'in the initial design, like we had that lead object that then uh gets like you create the signup off of it'

items.topic: Fields and buttons vary by status
items.statement: Kobi proposed that fields shown differ by status: in lead status only base intake info shows, and other buttons appear after the rep clicks a 'proceed to sign up' button that moves status to in progress.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um so if it's in the lead status, it'll just be like the handful of like base information that came in. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um and then when they progress like these buttons could be hidden and it these only show up once they click on like proceed to sign up button that'll move the status up to like in progress or something.

items.statement: Rep workspace uses filtered list views such as 'my leads' (lead status needing review, default) and pending/in-progress signups; progressed records drop off the leads view.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: like I would focus on creating filter views for like like these are my leads. / Joyce Kiddell: These are like my pending signups. / Kobi Kunasekaran: and then anything that's already progressed to the next stage will just be like removed from that list. And then we could have another one that's like uh leads that are or leads or signups that are in progress / Joyce Kiddell: Yep,

items.statement: Kobi said adding a lead stage to the existing signup object is limited rework and fairly quick, unlike adding a new object.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: like you've got what you need there to kind of I'm I'm assuming it's a bit of a rework / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh not too much. Not too much. Just based on what we're talking about. Like if we're introducing a new object and that is going to add a lot more rework in in terms of automation, but if we're just adding another stage um that yes, like it it'll be uh fairly

items.statement: WagerTech asked to group both queue views by player; Emily said it is important for usability. Kobi was not sure it is possible in Salesforce and will check.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: is for both Q views, if we can group it by player. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I I I don't know if that's actually possible in Salesforce. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I will double check.

items.topic: Spike player grouping and LWC with Jester
items.statement: Kobi will review player grouping / custom LWC console features with Jester and report back with feasibility, time and cost (a spike).
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: I'll run it by Jester and see what we can do and I'll get back to you. / Joyce Kiddell: but just kind of give us like a spike on like if it is costing like how much time is that going to take? Is it possible blah blah

items.topic: Custom LWC cost and mobile risk
items.statement: Kobi flagged that custom LWCs are expensive to build and maintain, have platform limits on record page placement, and may not port easily to mobile.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: It does give us the ability to like fully customize things, but it comes at a cost. Like it's uh one, it's expensive to build. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And another concern or potential risk with like custom LWCs is they don't necessarily port over to mobile easily.

items.topic: Fallback sort by player and side panel
items.statement: If grouping is not feasible, Joyce suggested sorting by player; Kobi suggested a right-side panel listing the player's other in-progress signups. Kobi will see what can be done.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: just like this is our like, you know, best case. If not, I do know it's possible to be able to sort by player. So, / Joyce Kiddell: like maybe we do that. / Kobi Kunasekaran: like if they want to work on the same player, we could have a panel on the right that's like here are all these other signups that uh the player also has in progress and they could click through those to work on the others. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Let me see what we can do.

items.statement: The signup record drops the path/chevron in favour of a simple status indicator, with queue quick-view colours mapped to status (for example flagged for fraud, past due). Kobi agreed.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: But basically like these colors would map to like whatever the status is here. Um and I to be honest I did away with like the chevron thing here. / Joyce Kiddell: But with this like it yeah I just I think a status just saying like did we flag it for fraud? You know is it past due? / Kobi Kunasekaran: But I'm with you. / Kobi Kunasekaran: This makes sense.

items.statement: Joyce said WagerTech could send some status ideas for the colour-coded indicators. No firm commitment or date.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: information. I don't know like what there's a couple like status ideas we could send your way.

items.topic: Reps edit only referral and proof
items.statement: On the signup record the rest is read-only context; reps input only the referral information and proof sections. The mockup's Edit button has no purpose; no other fields should be rep-editable.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: but the two sections that the rep would actually need to input are um items uh items specific to the refer information and the proof, right? / Kobi Kunasekaran: Like if are there specific fields beyond the ones that you've highlighted below under the referral information or proof that they should be able to edit? No. / Joyce Kiddell: No, absolutely not.

items.statement: The rep searches for the referrer by name; if not found, a pop-up modal lets them create the new person/referral record from the signup.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: And it like you would search for like the player name, and then if it exists, / Joyce Kiddell: then it just kind of like stays as that. Um, if not, then a a pop-up portal will like prompt you to create like a new person essentially. / Joyce Kiddell: but like you can create you could create it in the modal, / Kobi Kunasekaran: You can Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.

items.statement: The signup needs a secondary referrer field, as another lookup below the primary referrer.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: And then we added in like a bit of feedback that secondary we would want secondary refer in there too. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Yeah, we definitely need secondary refer. So, like I would imagine that's like another field. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Just another look up below.

items.topic: Payout type editable at signup level
items.statement: Payout type (bet credit vs cash) is the only referrer data point customizable at signup level. Other referrer data (currency, country) is static and edited on the referral record.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Um and then payout type. / Joyce Kiddell: customizable with the refer at like a signup level, / Joyce Kiddell: refer like um country, like all of that stuff is like more or less static. / Joyce Kiddell: So like if you do have to update that, you do it on the actual referral record, not on the signup you know. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I see. Okay.

items.statement: Payout amount, derived from the payout matrix based on referrer and payout type (not rep-entered), should be surfaced next to payout type.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Do we want to are we trying to display those here as well or like what happens after they select like bet credit or cash here? / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. I think payout amount is actually a good call to also surface. / Kobi Kunasekaran: But the payout amount like the reps aren't entering though, / Kobi Kunasekaran: right? It's just it comes from the the matrix. / Joyce Kiddell: Exactly.

items.statement: Joyce suggested an admin panel in Salesforce where admins configure payout values; values do not change day to day but are subject to change. Jumpr did not explicitly confirm the admin panel.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I think we should we should have some sort of admin panel that like admins are able to configure within / Joyce Kiddell: Salesforce somewhere, / Joyce Kiddell: but like it's not going to change on a day-to-day. / Emily Vandenberg: Yeah. It it it's subject to change like if we make decision but market

items.statement: Because payout values can change, payout information will be stamped as a snapshot by a flow when the rep chooses bet credit or cash, not pulled by formula, so old records do not change retroactively.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Or when they choose bet, credit or cash, we would have a flow that holds the information at the time that they're setting the record and it stamps it. So it's a snapshot. / Kobi Kunasekaran: then we would want to like capture the snapshot value instead of formulas. / Emily Vandenberg: Yep. / Kobi Kunasekaran: We can do that.
items.critic_note: Added context: Kobi said the snapshot method is more effort than a formula field, 'but not not crazy' (line 656).

items.topic: Secondary referrals tracked at referral level
items.statement: Secondary referrals pay on a milestone (about every 10 secondary referrals for a bet credit); reps only capture the secondary referrer on the signup. The count lives on the referral record, not the signup.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So for secondary refers, like if I remember correctly, it's just um counting against how many they've done. So it's like if they've done like 10 secondary refers, it's like a milestone that they have to hit in order to get like a $250 back credit. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, I guess like that that information would technically live at the referral level, / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah, exactly. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So it wouldn't be here on the sign
items.critic_note: Firmness kept for the referral-level tracking (Joyce: 'Yeah, exactly'). The milestone detail (every 10, bet credit amount) is not confirmed: Joyce said 'if I remember correctly' and Emily said Lena can confirm (line 667).

items.statement: Emily said ops will probably need the system to calculate secondary referrals and push them for payout at the threshold (every 10); Lena can confirm the exact rule.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: We pro we probably need a push cue of like when it hits the threshold joist like we would from an ops perspective there would need to be like it would need to assist in that like it would just kind of like um calculate and then at / Emily Vandenberg: threshold push so it' be like I think it's every I don't know Lena can kind of give it to you but we can and / Emily Vandenberg: then every 10 it gets like pushed up for payout.

items.statement: Kobi stated there is no payout object yet; it would track what has been paid out and what is pending.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And then we don't have the payout object or anything right now, / Kobi Kunasekaran: but I imagine that's where it would live. Like as you do the payouts, / Kobi Kunasekaran: you would create a record to keep track of what's been paid out and what's pending to be paid out.

items.statement: The referral record screen should show the number of primary and secondary referrals.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: it should have like number of like primary referrals and secondary referrals. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Yep. Okay.

items.statement: The wager proof is not always mandatory, so it is marked optional.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: so we talked about this yesterday and that like the wager proof is like not always like mandatory. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. / Joyce Kiddell: Like we try to like ingest that as much as possible. Um but uh that's the only reason why I kind of put it in optional

items.statement: Open whether a proof upload system will be built outside Salesforce; if so, Salesforce only needs a verified/missing status, with the date possibly prefilled from AI-scan metadata.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: brackets. Um the only question mark I still have I think with this box is um whether like we're planning on building a system like outside of Salesforce where you can actually upload proof. / Joyce Kiddell: then it's like you just kind of need the tick there that says like verified or missing, right?

items.statement: As an interim bridge, each proof gets a URL field; populating it sets that proof to verified and counts toward 'X of 2 proofs verified'. When the integration is built, the fields can be hidden while the interface stays the same.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: we instead of the free text field that you have there for the date, we could have a field for the URL for each of those proofs, the same as you do in your spreadsheet as they if they fill in the URL, / Kobi Kunasekaran: then the status will be set to verified. Um, and that'll like that'll count up the one out of two proofs verified. / Joyce Kiddell: that's a great idea. Yep.
items.critic_note: summary_agreement changed to 'no': Gemini Decisions says populating the URL updates 'the record status to verified'; transcript says the proof's status is set to verified and counts toward '1 of 2 proofs verified'.

items.statement: Joyce asked for a date field per proof and Kobi said it can be done, but Emily noted reps do not record a date against proofs today (only a signup date). No final decision on a per-proof date.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: I think we did we still need a date field, / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, we can do that. / Emily Vandenberg: Do we care about the date? / Joyce Kiddell: Oh, we don't. I thought we did in our login. / Emily Vandenberg: It's not like a fraud scenario, but they're not recording the actual date of um against the proofs.

items.statement: Vertical must be captured on the lead/signup, sourced from the related deal (same vertical as the deal).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: just make sure vertical is in there because like we should be able to pull that out of the API. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah, that that I mean I figured it'll come from the deal. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Uh but yeah, yeah, we can do that because it it should be the same same vertical as the deal that the signup is related to, / Joyce Kiddell: Yes. Yeah.

items.topic: Distinct agency and affiliate signup dates
items.statement: There must be two distinct fields: agency signup date (from the click payload, view-only to reps) and affiliate signup date (entered manually by the rep).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: up for our internal website versus when did they sign up for the affiliate site. So call it whatever, / Joyce Kiddell: but like they have to be two distinct fields. / Kobi Kunasekaran: it won't be editable by the reps in this page. Like, it'll just be view only. But then for this uh affiliate signup date that one they are going to enter in / Joyce Kiddell: Yes.

items.topic: Agency signup date lives on player
items.statement: Agency signup date should live at the player level and be referable, and can come out of the signup queue view; the rep-entered signup date moves into the editable area.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: so it can come out of this view but it needs to live against the player and you have to be able to refer to / Joyce Kiddell: Yeah. Yes. / Joyce Kiddell: Okay. Okay. We're aligned.

items.statement: Joyce asked for a progress indicator (for example '0 of 1') on the editable blocks, a check on each completed step, and a header indicator of what is left on the signup record.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: So, can we have like a progress thing where it's like zero of one kind of thing? / Joyce Kiddell: Um and then maybe like after you complete it, there's like a quick check on each step like I don't know.

items.topic: Flag and archive via screen flow
items.statement: Archive and Flag actions each open a screen flow modal to pick a reason code and add notes, replacing the current checkbox plus dropdown fraud flag.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um but like both like in this case archive and flag uh would also have reason codes. So the instead of I think in your current screen there is like a checkbox and then like a drop down or whatever for the fraud flag. / Joyce Kiddell: I'd like to do a screen flow or whatever they're called um where it's like it pops up a modal you / Kobi Kunasekaran: Sure. Yeah.
items.supersedes_hint: Replaces the current build's fraud flag checkbox + dropdown

items.statement: Flag is a blanket for anything the rep wants to highlight, combining won't-do and fraud (for example suspicious gameplay, hedging). Archive is for non-alarming reasons (not responding, cannot access account). Each has its own reason set; the exact split is still to be worked out.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So flag isn't necessarily fraud, right? / Joyce Kiddell: but like fraud would be part of this, / Joyce Kiddell: And that like I'm I'm I'm just combining the concept of won't do and and fraud into one. Um just like flag blanket and then archive like this one would be more like / Joyce Kiddell: like you know the players not responding or they can't get into their account. Like we have to figure out how to separate those.

items.statement: Flagged records go to a separate view for ops review; archived records get their own filterable tab.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: no. I think like the reason I also want flag separate is that like I want those to go to like a separate view for ops or like something for them to be able to like review, / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Joyce Kiddell: right? Archive in my mind just creates like another tab over here where it's like you can filter for archived

items.topic: Exclusive end states with reason sets
items.statement: A signup ends in exactly one of flagged, archived or complete, held in a single status, with a different reason set for archive versus flag. A flagged or archived signup is not past due.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: so in my mind it has to either be flagged or archived or complete. / Kobi Kunasekaran: So then it's it's all still like a status then because the status will be they can it could only be one of those things. Um but there's an option but if they choose archive then we have a different set of reasons that / Kobi Kunasekaran: they should select versus for flag it's a different set of reasons that they should select. / Emily Vandenberg: is not passed due. Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Correct.

items.statement: Status automation: past due follows logic for in-progress records; Complete could be set automatically when all required fields are filled. Joyce wants a manual Complete with an 'are you sure' modal for edge cases and ops visibility. Because Complete triggers payout, they will work it through with Lena.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So it yes in theory if we if we know all the fields that need to be filled out we could automatically move a sign up to the complete status assuming it's not flagged or anything like that. / Emily Vandenberg: cuz like complete will trigger payment. Um, right. Like we the way I think of it is like it moves into a payout. / Emily Vandenberg: So I think the automation makes sense. Yeah, I think we should talk about it a bit more with that one. We should kind of probably like work through with Lena.

items.statement: Open: which edge cases justify manually completing a signup without all required fields; to be worked through with Lena (WagerTech ops).
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Um just so like we don't necessarily block the rep if they have like a good reason to move it along. Like I just it might be something that we have to talk through with Lena.

items.statement: The status shown on the record is display only (not a dropdown) and locked; the top-right controls are actions.
items.quote: Emily Vandenberg: It's not a drop down or anything. / Kobi Kunasekaran: we can lock it down so that Yeah, / Joyce Kiddell: those are those are all actions. Yes.

items.statement: Flagging gets a sub-status lifecycle from the PRD (suspected, under review, confirmed, dismissed) so ops can track the flag through review.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: But then if something is flagged that could be a sub status that it's flagged. I think we had like a in your PRD you had that right? / Kobi Kunasekaran: uh you had like uh suspected, under review, confirmed, dismissed and we could have that so that whatever reason that they're flagging for um we're tracking that life cycle there. / Joyce Kiddell: Yes. Okay. Sure. Yeah.

items.statement: The 'Won't Do' status is removed. Primary statuses become lead, new, in progress, completed, archived, plus flagged.
items.quote: Joyce Kiddell: Yes. Okay. Sure. Yeah. And can we just kill won't do though? / Joyce Kiddell: Like if like as a word like if if it's actually won't do just do like archived and then / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Yeah, I like that. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Well, sorry. Sorry. If if we kill Wu the in the primary status, so we're going to have like lead, new, uh, in progress, completed, and archived. Like, do we want us something for like fraud as well specifically / Joyce Kiddell: flags. Flags.
items.supersedes_hint: Kobi's model (line 972) had primary statuses new lead, in progress, completed, won't do; Won't Do now replaced by Archived and Flagged

items.topic: Design status workflow, demo next week
items.statement: Kobi to think through the signup statuses and workflow, and next week show how a lead progresses to a signup and how a signup moves to each end route, screen by screen.

Yeah.

items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So once OP releases it, if it's confirmed, then that updates the primary status to won't do with the status reason something like

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Payout snapshot values for signups The system will utilize a flow to capture and stamp payout snapshot values at the time of record creation to avoid retroactive changes from formula updates.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Or when they choose bet, credit or cash, we would have a flow that holds the information at the time that they're setting the record and it stamps it. So it's a snapshot.
gemini_disagreements.why: Trigger differs: transcript ties the snapshot to when the rep chooses bet credit or cash (payout type can change at signup level), not to record creation.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: Proof verification via URL fields Proof verification will be implemented by using URL fields that automatically update the record status to verified when populated.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: then the status will be set to verified. Um, and that'll like that'll count up the one out of two proofs verified.
gemini_disagreements.why: Gemini says the record status becomes verified; transcript says each proof's status is set to verified and counts toward '1 of 2 proofs verified'. The signup record status is not changed by this.

gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than transcript for migration: Emily said 'we can talk about that early next week'; no session was set. Only the Monday 10 a.m. Deal Rep Assignment session was booked.

notes: Focused UI/design working session on the Sign-Up (lead/signup) record using Joyce's clickable mockup. Key outcomes: single Signup object with lead status (no separate Lead object); Won't Do removed in favour of Archived and Flagged with separate reason sets and a flag sub-status lifecycle; payout snapshot via flow; proof URL fields mark verified; distinct agency vs affiliate signup dates; vertical from deal. Player grouping and console LWC left bar pending Kobi/Jester feasibility spike. Deal Rep Assignment session Monday 2026-07-20 10:00 (Joyce booked). No Jira keys spoken. Rule 5: skipped utilization/hours report exchange (lines ~115-126) and budget wording in Emily's scope check (line 1056); items cite only delivery content. Gemini Details section also treated as summary. 'Kobe' = Kobi, 'adjuster' = Jester [ASR].
